goal: The foundations, while the brain is fresh. By four o'clock you can write a complete Java program from a blank page, braces and semicolons and all, and trace one line by line to say exactly what it prints.
drill: The objective questions on topics 1 and 2 sit at the end of What Java Is and Input and Output. Then write the program skeleton from memory, three times.

window: Wednesday evening, 6:30 pm to 10:30 pm, after the Python paper
goal: Control structures, which Section A of the paper is built from. Start with fifteen minutes, book shut, writing down everything you remember from Monday. Then the four lessons, and the for to while conversion that was worth half of a ten mark part last time.
drill: The control structures questions at the end of For to While. If you are wrecked after two papers today, stop at nine; this is the one block you can cut short.

goal: Section B and Section C: methods that return, and the array walk. Then sit the 2025/2026 paper's questions in your book before you read a model answer. This is the shape your paper takes: one question from each section.
drill: In the paper, choose the dry run or loop conversion in Section A, the ARRAY question in Section B, and switch with methods in Section C.

window: Thursday, 11:00 am to 1:30 pm, only what you have time for, in this order
goal: Everything else, ranked by how likely it is to earn you marks. Break and continue and overloading first, since both appear in Section A. Then strings. The object and exception lessons are for the objective half only: read them if you are ahead, skip them if not. Finish with the reference card, and stop at half past one whatever you have reached.
drill: Eat something before the paper. The API card in the reference is the last thing you read.
